summary: Remote WebSocket peer holds interactive shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade control over the installer's host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent connects to a configured WebSocket server and, after an initial shared-secret handshake, dispatches server-sent messages to handlers that grant the remote peer full control of the installer's machine. 'terminal_create' / 'terminal_input' messages spawn a real bash or PowerShell PTY via node-pty and write remote payloads verbatim into it, giving the peer an interactive shell with the user's privileges. message-router.js also routes 'write_file', 'create_file', 'delete_files', 'move_files', 'copy_files', and 'git_push' messages to workbench handlers that mutate the local filesystem and push to configured git remotes with no per-action consent prompt. An 'upgrade_agent' message triggers handleUpgradeAgent, which resolves @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest from the npm registry and spawns a detached bash/bat script that runs 'npm install' (or 'npm i -g') followed by a systemd/launchd/PM2 restart, letting the server push a new package version (and any postinstall) onto the host at a moment the operator did not choose. service/linux.js additionally prepends '~/.local/bin' and '~/.npm-global/bin' to PATH in the installed service environment. The remote-controlled shell and filesystem channels give whoever controls the WebSocket server full-host RCE over any machine running the agent, and the self-upgrade path provides an on-demand code-update channel through the same channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
